title: Pendulum, 40 cm

source.credit: Rendered by Ansatz with known physics (a school practical: true length 0.40 m, g = 9.81 m/s²)

caveats: animated illustration rather than filmed real motion, so scale may not be physical

reference.basis: standard A4 sheet long side used as scale reference

slow_motion.evidence: no on-screen text or visual indication of slow motion

subjects.description: small orange spherical bob on a black string suspended from a bar

observation.what_happens: An orange ball suspended by a string swings back and forth below a fixed support. It moves from the right side through the bottom of its arc to the left and back again, repeating continuously through the clip.

calibration.note: white paper = 0.297 m (standard A4 sheet long side used as scale reference) spans 204 px in SAM's mask

given: scale: white paper = 0.297 m (standard A4 sheet long side used as scale reference) spans 204 px in SAM's mask, known to ±6%
pendulum length L = 0.402 m, measured from the radius of the swing with the ruler: hold L fixed and measure g
reasoning: Theta oscillates +-0.17 rad with ~1.27 s period and r is constant at 0.402 m, matching 2*pi*sqrt(L/g) for a pendulum; amplitude looks almost constant. Candidates keep exact sin(theta) with fixed L to measure g, from undamped textbook to linear viscous to quadratic air drag to test which loss predicts the held-back 30%.

law.title: Textbook pendulum (small angles)
law.summary: Swings like a simple harmonic oscillator: angular acceleration proportional to the angle.

fitted.title: Textbook pendulum (small angles)
fitted.summary: Swings like a simple harmonic oscillator: angular acceleration proportional to the angle.

caveats: Scale from A4 sheet is known to about ±6%, so absolute g carries that uncertainty.
Length L was held fixed from the video ruler, not fitted.
Quadratic air drag fit almost as well, so linear vs quadratic damping is not strongly distinguished.
critique.finding: It swings as a damped pendulum with gravity g = {g} and light friction {gamma}. The swing shrinks just a little each pass.
critique.headline: The hanging ball swings on, gently slowed by air
critique.why_it_won: It matches the steady fade of each swing better than the quadratic drag law which expects faster swings to fade much quicker.

headline: The hanging ball swings on, gently slowed by air
finding: It swings as a damped pendulum with gravity g = 9.86 ± 0.59 m/s² and light friction 0.0306 ± 0.0028 1/s. The swing shrinks just a little each pass.

eyeball.confidence: low-medium, limited pixel scale and ~7 swings in 8 s video
eyeball.law_in_words: Small-angle simple pendulum period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) with L scaled from the 0.297 m paper long side pivot to bob centre, T timed frame-by-frame over ~300 frames at 37.5 fps, and viscous damped amplitude envelope ~ exp(-gamma t/2) from theta_double_dot + gamma theta_dot + (g/L) theta = 0.
